bio-text:
I am an archivist at the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA), currently seconded to the National Archives as Head of the Northeast Regional Office (2025–). I coordinate the Farinha and Arquivos da UFBA projects. I am interested in the interfaces between Archival Science, Digital Humanities, Hacker Culture, and Artificial Intelligence applied to archives.

Since 2024, I have been working at LABHDUFBA (Digital Humanities Laboratory at UFBA). I was coordinator of CRIDI (Study Group on Culture, Representation, and Digital Information) between 2019 and 2026, a group I have been a member of since 2008, currently inactive. My trajectory combines archival practice — working in records management, digital preservation, and archival description — with applied research in AI, network analysis, and data visualization applied to documentary collections.

about-bio-p1: Master's in Information Science and Bachelor's in Archival Science from the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA). He currently holds the position of Head of the Northeast Regional Office (ERE-NE) of the National Archives (2025–) and is a UFBA civil servant, working as an archivist on secondment to the National Archives. He coordinates the projects Farinha, free software for creating platforms for access to permanent archives and memorials, and Arquivos da UFBA, a platform for integration and access to the archives and collections of the Federal University of Bahia.
about-bio-p2: His career has focused on collection management, technical processing of archival information, and the development of access, outreach, and innovation initiatives. He has experience in archival description, information representation, and development of digital platforms for archival access, including initiatives using artificial intelligence (agents and RAG).
about-bio-p3: Since 2024, he has been working at LABHDUFBA (Digital Humanities Laboratory at UFBA). He was coordinator of CRIDI (Study Group on Culture, Representation, and Digital Information) between 2019 and 2026, a group he has been a member of since 2008. He also participated in the research groups GEPICC (2003–2008) and GEPINDI (2004–2007).
about-bio-p4: His work spans the interfaces between Archival Science, Digital Humanities, access to information, hacker culture, and technologies applied to archives, with applied research in AI, network analysis, and data visualization applied to documentary collections. He is a ham radio operator (PU6RIC), of Brazilian and Portuguese nationality, and was an elected delegate to the 1st CNARQ and an appointed delegate to the 2nd CNARQ (National Conference on Archives).
